constraint: Must maintain dental implant function within clinical specifications
mechanism: Loss of vertical dimension of occlusion (VDO) leads to altered occlusal forces and increased mechanical stress on dental implants, accelerating wear and malfunction; restoring proper VDO through occlusal rehabilitation rebalances forces and mitigates implant wear.
intervention: Implement occlusal rehabilitation protocols (e.g., occlusal veneers, full-mouth rehabilitation, or the Dahl concept) to reestablish the correct vertical dimension of occlusion, thereby normalizing occlusal loading on dental implants and preventing excessive wear.
expected_effect: Reduced implant surface wear and mechanical failure, improved long-term implant stability and function within clinical specifications.
falsification_test: In a cohort of patients with dental implants and confirmed VDO loss, randomly assign half to receive occlusal rehabilitation restoring VDO and half to no intervention; measure implant wear (e.g., via 3D scanning or radiographic assessment) and functional failure rates over 2–5 years. If the intervention group shows no significant reduction in wear or malfunction compared to controls, the mechanism is falsified.

Despite its profound impact on orofacial function, esthetics, masticatory efficiency, and oral health-related quality of life, no universally accepted operational definition, diagnostic threshold, or treatment protocol currently exists.
